partner_context.their_ambition: Qatar's Ministry of Transport is building a modern, multimodal network under its Comprehensive Transport Plan — and water is explicitly part of it. The MOT's Water Taxi project has already delivered its first-phase terminals at Lusail, The Pearl and the Corniche, with eco-friendly waterborne transport as a stated goal. Katara and Qatar Tourism, both prior Navier contacts, own the experience and destination layer.
partner_context.their_pressure: Doha's growth is concentrated on a compact, traffic-dense bay — West Bay, Lusail, The Pearl, Katara — where the fastest line between two points is across the water, not around it. Qatar wants a flagship, sustainable, world-class system befitting its post-2022 ambitions.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the premium, zero-emission, software-defined edge of the water network Qatar is already building — turning the new water-taxi infrastructure into a fast, smooth, foiling system from day one.

hero.title: Qatar × Navier — the foiling water network for Doha Bay
hero.subtitle: Qatar is already building the water-taxi infrastructure. Navier makes it fly.
hero.what_we_do_together: We bring software-defined foiling vessels to Qatar's new water-taxi network — a premium, zero-emission system across Doha Bay's most congested and most iconic corridors. The Ministry of Transport brings the terminals, the mandate and the network; Katara and Qatar Tourism bring the destinations; Navier brings the fleet and the playbook proven in the Maldives.

why_now: The MOT has completed phase-one water-taxi infrastructure — Lusail Ferry Terminal plus Pearl and Corniche stops — and is explicit about eco-friendly waterborne transport. The terminals are going in; the question is what runs on them. A ~100-vessel Navier network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026). This is the moment to specify foiling as the standard.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the MOT's Comprehensive Transport Plan as the marine mode — integrated with the Doha Metro, tram and bus network, sharing the new water-taxi terminals, and tying the airport, the Corniche and the islands into one journey.

journeys_unlocked.today: 20–35 min along a congested bay-front road.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A smooth foiling run straight up the bay in minutes.

differentiation.vs_ferry: Conventional water taxis are slow and diesel. Foiling vessels are fast, near-silent and zero-emission — a flagship-grade ride for a flagship destination.
differentiation.vs_candela: Foiling competitors validate the category for Gulf authorities. Navier adds a software-defined, on-demand premium tier plus Quanta-LR hybrid range for the longer Gulf legs (e.g. Doha ↔ the Eastern Province) with no charging infrastructure.
differentiation.navier_moat: Software-defined, autonomy-ready, a Turkey factory for regional supply, and a ~100-vessel at-scale network proving the model in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: Qatar is already building the water network.
proof_points.evidence: MOT Water Taxi project phase-one complete: Lusail Ferry Terminal + Pearl + Corniche stops; eco-friendly waterborne transport stated goal.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for Qatar?
objections.response: The entire Doha Bay network — West Bay, Lusail, The Pearl, Banana Island, the airport waterfront — sits within a few nautical miles, deep inside Pioneer II all-electric range. Quanta-LR covers any cross-Gulf ambition with no charging infrastructure.
Climate-controlled cabins, dramatically lower energy per mile, and scheduling flexibility around peak summer — the same as every Gulf mobility mode.
Software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class path, and an operating record in the US and the Maldives.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Doha Bay beachhead
featured_routes: Old Doha Port ↔ Katara Cultural Village
phases.rationale: Launch on the exact corridors the MOT's new water-taxi terminals already serve — the busiest, most iconic stretch of Doha Bay.
phases.narrative: Six Pioneer II vessels on the MOT's new water-taxi corridors — West Bay, Lusail, The Pearl, Katara — proving a premium, zero-emission foiling system on the bay Qatar is already wiring for water.

phases.label: Phase 2 — The full Doha network
featured_routes: Corniche ↔ Al Wakrah ↔ Al Khor — coastal extension
phases.rationale: Extend from the bay core to the airport, the island resorts and the coastal towns — the complete marine mode of the Comprehensive Transport Plan.
phases.narrative: We complete the network: airport-to-hotel foiling arrivals, on-demand Banana Island access, and a coastal extension to Al Wakrah and Al Khor — Qatar's flagship water system, integrated with metro and tram.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, the Maldives-proven network playbook, captain training and the first-of-class certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The MOT's water-taxi terminals, network mandate and metro/tram integration; Katara and Qatar Tourism's destinations and events.
the_ask.next_step: A Doha Bay pilot on the new water-taxi corridors, co-specified with the Ministry of Transport.

close.title: Qatar built the terminals. Navier makes the network fly.
close.body: The bay core proves it; the airport, the islands and the coast complete it — a flagship, zero-emission foiling network for Doha, integrated into the transport plan Qatar is already building.
